newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian labour leader needs more medical tests.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian labour leader needs more medical tests.

text.p: Jailed Indonesian labour leader Mucthar Pakpahan will undergo further medical tests next week after a recent biopsy of a lung tumor proved inconclusive, one of his lawyers said on Saturday.
"Today I was told the biopsy test was not representative, so another biopsy needs to be done next Wednesday at the Dharmais Cancer Hospital," lawyer Luthfie Hakim told Reuters.
The hospital is run by the Dharmais charitable foundation controlled by President Suharto.

Hakim said Pakpahan, head of the unrecognised Indonesian Labour Welfare Union (SBSI), would return to hospital from his jail cell because an apparent error in the biopsy done at Cikini hospital on Thursday afternoon made it inconclusive.

"It is not clear if it was a technical or human error," he said. "He still feels pain throughout the right side of his body and he will also have a Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) test at the Cipto Mangunkusumo Hospital on Monday," Hakim added.
A test completed last week showed the tumor in Pakpahan's right lung was bigger than on the x-ray image on which it was first detected, he said.

Pakpahan had his first biopsy two days after the U.S Assistant Secretary of State for Democracy, Human Rights and Labour, John Shattuck, saw him in the private Cikini hospital in central Jakarta on Tuesday.
"Mr Pakpahan is seriously ill and requires urgent medical care," Shattuck told reporters on the island of Bali on Friday.
Shattuck said he received assurances from government officials that Pakpahan would receive the necessary medical care.

However, Hakim said Shattuck invited Pakpahan to seek medical treatment in the United States. The labor leader said that he would request his release from jail and permission to travel to the United States.

Pakpahan was one of a number of activists arrested and charged with subversion after rioting in the capital Jakarta last July in which at least five people died. Subversion carries the maximum penalty of death in Indonesia.
He has also been concurrently serving a previous four-year sentence for inciting riots that was suspended by the Supreme Court in 1995 but reimposed late last year in a highly unusual review.
His subversion trial was suspended until further notice after his medical problems surfaced two weeks ago.
